description: baseline

Replace the template with a full airbench port in submissions/arena/. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv (eigenvectors computed in prepare from training images), Dirac-initialized convs, widths 128/384/576 with 3 convs per group, BN with a 64x bias LR, and a GAP+linear head scaled for 100 classes. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD at batch 1024 with lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, Lookahead and a triangular LR. Training: label smoothing 0.3, alternating flip, random crop with 2 px translate, 8.5 epochs, no TTA. The full uint8 dataset lives on the GPU with augmentation done there. Use fp16 autocast and channels_last. torch.compile the train step in build and warm it up on synthetic data; use drop_last so batch shapes stay fixed. Eval uses an uncompiled (or dynamic=True) path so any B from 1 to 1024 avoids slow recompiles. Log prepare and train time separately.

Same as the airbench port, with only the epoch count raised from 8.5 to 9.5. The triangular LR schedule stretches to match, and nothing else changes. This hedges the thin margin that the TTA ban leaves.

Re-run the current incumbent airbench config unchanged, as a pure replicate, and record per-seed accuracies and per-trial prepare/train times. This calibrates the noise floor that every later delta is judged against.

On the feasible airbench incumbent, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768) and cut epochs from the incumbent count to 7.5, with the LR schedule rescaled. Everything else is held fixed.

On the incumbent, compute the patch-whitening covariance from a random 5000-image subset (drawn with the trial-seeded generator inside prepare) instead of all 50k. Also make the dataset transfer a single bulk uint8 copy to the GPU, with normalization fused into the train step. Report prepare time.

Throughput ablation on the incumbent: switch the torch.compile mode from default to max-autotune, with autotuning done fully in the untimed build on synthetic batches of the exact training shapes (full batch plus any eval shapes used in train). Check with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that zero recompiles happen in the timed region, which also covers H3.2.1.

Explore: on the incumbent architecture, replace Nesterov SGD on the conv weights with Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 Newton-Schulz steps, batch 2000). Biases, BN and the head stay on SGD. Use the same epoch budget, tuned so wall time matches the SGD incumbent.

Exploit, following E004's contingency. On the current incumbent (E006: subset whitening, max-autotune compile, fp16, channels_last), widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768). Set epochs to 9.25 and stretch the triangular LR to match. Everything else stays fixed: lr 9.0, wd 0.012, ls 0.3, Lookahead, alternating flip, batch 1024 with drop_last. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step.

Exploit, cutting per-step cost where it is concentrated. E004's post-mortem found that the high-resolution group-1 layers (32x32 and 16x16) dominate step time. Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2 (keep the pooling position and the 128 width). Run it on the best 768-wide config (I-768 at 9.25 epochs if that run is kept; otherwise on the incumbent), keeping the same epochs and everything else.

Explore, as an alternative way to cheapen group 1. Keep 3 convs in group 1 but narrow its width from 128 to 96 channels (96/384/768, or 96/384/576 on the incumbent if the 768 run isn't kept). The whitening conv output and the group-2 input adjust to match. Same epochs, LR rescaled only as airbench's width-independent scaling dictates (unchanged).
Explore: on the incumbent, train the first ~50% of epochs on 24 px random crops (downscaled from 32 px on the GPU), then 32 px for the rest. Compile and warm up both shapes in build.
Explore. On the incumbent config, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 and change nothing else. This is a decisive test of H1.3.1, which has never been tested.

Explore. Add loss-based data filtering. During the second half of training, keep the per-example loss computed in the forward pass. Each epoch, drop the 25% lowest-loss examples from the previous epoch, so second-half epochs have fewer batches. Batches stay fixed at 1024 with drop_last, so no new shapes appear. The losses are a byproduct of training (no extra forward passes), and the selection runs on the GPU with the trial-seeded generator. Keep the LR schedule defined over the total number of steps.

Exploit; this combines the E009 near-miss with extra epochs. Start from the E007 Muon incumbent (128/384/576, Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 / 3 NS steps, batch 2000, ls 0.3, alternating flip, max-autotune, subset whitening). Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2, exactly as in E009 (same pooling position, width 128). Raise epochs from 9.0 to 9.5 (about 238 steps) and stretch the LR schedule to match. Change nothing else. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step and per-seed accuracy.

Exploit; this is E011's contingency. Progressive resizing on the Muon incumbent, with more total epochs. Use 10.5 epochs in total. Train the first 50% of epochs on whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate; AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as in E011) and the rest at 32 px. Define the LR schedule over total steps. Compile with dynamic=False and warm up both shapes in build, so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Keep everything else at E007.

On the E007 Muon incumbent at 9.0 epochs, remove Lookahead and replace the triangular warmup+decay schedule with linear decay from peak to 0, with no warmup, for both the Muon and SGD groups. That is airbench94_muon style. Keep lr, momentum, batch and epochs fixed. Make the change in one run, because both components are SGD-era carryovers.

Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, switch to batch 1536 with Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 (Hiverge settings). Use the same 9.0 epochs (drop_last, so about 292 steps) and scale the SGD-group lr linearly with batch size. Warm up the new batch shape in build.

Throughput, numerically near-equivalent. Batch Newton-Schulz across conv weights by grouping same-shape weights into one batched matmul call. Use torch._foreach ops for the SGD updates on biases, BN and the head. Capture the full train step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD) in a CUDA graph with static input buffers, and warm it up in build on synthetic data. Pass the LR schedule as a GPU tensor so per-step LR changes need no recapture. prepare resets all parameter and state tensors in place.

Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, add a weight EMA that covers about the last epoch (decay about 0.99 per step at batch 2000, updated only in the final ~25% of steps). Also apply the EMA to the BN running statistics. Evaluate with the EMA weights. Run the EMA update as a single foreach op inside the compiled step. Reset the EMA in prepare.

Exploit: add progressive resizing to the E018 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 9.5 epochs, 0.7571 @ 8.16 s). This is E015's contingency moved onto the faster, higher-margin base. Train 11 epochs in total. Epochs 1-5 use whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head pooling as in E011/E015). Epochs 6-11 run at 32 px. Define the LR schedule (triangular plus Lookahead, as in the incumbent) over total steps. Batch 1536 with drop_last at both resolutions. Capture one CUDA graph per resolution in build and warm both on synthetic data, so nothing recompiles or recaptures in the timed region. Everything else stays at E018. Log per-phase ms/step.

Exploit the margin and measure the epoch slope on the current recipe. On E018, change only the epoch count, from 9.5 to 9.25 (32 steps/epoch at batch 1536 with drop_last, so 296 steps instead of 304), with the LR schedule stretched to match. Nothing else changes. The result gives the pp-per-second exchange rate on the graphed batch-1536 net, the reference for scoring every later per-step cut.

Explore whether smaller Muon batches keep buying accuracy now that per-step overhead is graphed away. E017 showed 2000 -> 1536 gave +0.16 pp at unchanged per-image cost. On E018, switch to batch 1024: Muon lr 0.205*sqrt(1024/1536) = 0.167 and momentum 0.70, with the SGD-group lr scaled linearly with batch. Keep 9.5 epochs (48 steps/epoch, 456 steps). Recapture the CUDA graph at the new batch shape in build.

Explore the next group-1 cut, extending E009's depth cut. On E018, reduce group 1 from 2 convs to 1, keeping only the 32x32 whitening-output -> 128 conv followed by pool/BN/GELU, and removing the remaining 16x16 128->128 conv. Raise epochs from 9.5 to 10.25 to compensate. Also record a one-step torch.profiler breakdown (conv vs BN/activation/pool kernels per stage) in the smoke test, which tests H2.4.1.

Exploit, cheapening the per-step Muon cost (~2 ms/step of GPU time per the E018 profile, the same at 24 and 32 px). On the E021 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 5 epochs at 24 px + 5.75 at 32 px, 0.7552 @ 7.62 s), replace the 3-step Newton-Schulz with Turbo-Muon-style almost-orthogonal preconditioning followed by 2 NS steps (C0008/C0009). Before NS, rescale X's columns by 1/sqrt of the row sums of |X^T X|, inside the batched NS call. Keep the same NS coefficients for the 2 remaining steps, and keep lr, momentum and everything else fixed. Recapture both CUDA graphs in build. Log ms/step per phase.

Exploit and test the untested intermediate-resolution step. On E021, change the resolution schedule from 5x24 px + 5.75x32 px to 5x24 px + 2x28 px + 4x32 px (11 epochs in total), with the LR schedule (triangle plus Lookahead) defined over total steps. Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate, as for 24 px, and keep AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in the head. Batch 1536 with drop_last at all three shapes. Capture and warm up a third CUDA graph (28 px) in build so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.

Explore, following C0012 (EfficientNetV2: scale regularization with image size). On E021 at a fixed epoch schedule, weaken regularization only in the 24 px phase. Use label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 and crop translation of 1 px instead of 2, applied before downscaling, during epochs 1-5. The 32 px phase stays at ls 0.3 and 2 px translate. Pass the ls value through the CUDA graph as a GPU scalar tensor, or capture the low-res graph with its own constant, so nothing is recaptured in the timed region. Time should be unchanged.

Noise calibration on the current incumbent, with no recipe change. Add an internal salt to the data-order/augmentation generator (the trial seeds stay 0, 1, 2) and run E021 with salt=1. Compare against E021's 0.7552 (salt 0) and log per-seed accuracies. This replaces I028, which was calibrated on E018, now superseded. The margin on the current tip (+0.22 pp) is the binding constraint for every remaining time cut.

Exploit and add margin. On the E025 incumbent (5x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with momentum 0.655, Turbo preconditioning plus 2 NS steps, CUDA graphs per resolution, Lookahead and triangle), raise the Muon peak lr by 1.25x, from 0.205 to 0.256, and change nothing else. The SGD groups, momentum, schedule shape and resolution schedule stay fixed. The LR lives in the GPU schedule tensor, so the graphs need no recapture. Rationale: the E024 note says Turbo preconditioning shrank the effective update on the big layers by about 1/3, and the inherited Hiverge lr was tuned for a 3/3/3 CIFAR-10 net without resizing. Run salt 0 (official) and also salt 1, so the comparison is against the pooled E025/E027 estimate of 0.7533 and not E025's single draw of 0.7539.

Exploit by removing high-resolution backward work that carries little accuracy. On E025, train the whitening-conv bias only during the 24 px phase (epochs 1-5). In the 28 px and 32 px phases, detach the whitening-layer output (after its activation) before group 1. Autograd then skips the dgrad of the first 128-channel conv and the whitening BN/activation backward at the highest resolutions. In the optimizer, drop the whitening bias from those phases' parameter list, or zero its LR. The 28 and 32 px graphs are captured in build with the detach already in place, and the 24 px graph is unchanged, so no new graph count and no recapture in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.

Exploit the resolution ladder one rung lower. On E025, run epochs 1-2 at 20 px instead of 24 px, so the schedule becomes 2x20 + 3x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 (11 epochs in total, the same LR schedule over total steps). Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate after the 2 px translate crop, as for 24/28 px, and keep the AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head. Batch 1536 with drop_last. Capture and warm up a 4th CUDA graph (20 px) in build. Rationale: the first epochs learn coarse features and the triangle is still warming up, so resolution matters least there. E020 and E025 both gained from cheaper early pixels.

Explore cutting the fixed per-step cost (Muon ~1.5 ms/step after E024, plus Lookahead and launch costs) in the cheap low-res phase. On E025, use batch 3072 in the 24 px phase only (epochs 1-5, 16 steps/epoch with drop_last instead of 32). In that phase, scale the Muon lr by sqrt(2) (0.29) and the SGD-group lr linearly (2x), with momentum unchanged. Keep batch 1536 at 28 and 32 px. Define the LR schedule per step over the new total step count, keeping the same epoch boundaries. Capture the 24 px graph at batch 3072 in build (one graph per resolution, as now).

Measure the exchange rate and build a safe-margin fallback. On E025, add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (5x24 + 2x28 + 4.5x32, LR schedule over total steps) and change nothing else. A 0.5-epoch step is about 2x the measured trajectory noise, so unlike the 0.25-epoch trim of E021 its effect can be read. The result fixes the pp/s line against which E024-style cuts and the 20 px and batch ideas are scored. It also gives the config to fall back on if the official 40-seed mean of E025 looks marginal (pooled 0.7533).

Exploit: remove more high-resolution backward work, extending E029. On E030 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 0.7533 @ 6.95 s), freeze the whole first group-1 conv block (conv 32x32 whitening-output -> 128, pool, BN, GELU) during the 4 epochs at 32 px. In the 32 px CUDA graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv, and drop that conv's weight and its BN affine params from that phase's Muon/SGD parameter lists (or zero their LR). E029 already skips this conv's dgrad. This change also removes its wgrad at 32x32 and the BN/GELU/pool backward at 32x32 and 16x16. BN stays in train mode, so running stats keep updating at 32 px. Capture the modified 32 px graph in build, keeping the same graph count with no recapture in the timed region. Log ms/step per phase. Rationale (FreezeOut-style): the first conv sees the whitened patches and converges earliest. The 28 px and 20/24 px phases (7 epochs) still train it.
salt-1 companion of E033 (calibration only, never kept)

Exploit: cut Muon's fixed per-step cost (about 1.5 ms of ~350 steps, roughly 7% of train time) once more. On E030, keep Turbo/AOL column preconditioning but run 1 Newton-Schulz quintic step instead of 2. Use the same coefficients, the same lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, and the per-step weight renorm unchanged. Recapture all 4 graphs in build. Rationale: E024 showed Muon is insensitive to singular-value spread in [0.67, 1.2], and E028 showed accuracy is flat in lr over 0.205-0.256. The per-step renorm also fixes the overall update scale, so a less exact orthogonalization may cost nothing. Log Muon ms/step.

Explore which pixels buy margin most cheaply, as a companion to the rebased I039. On E030, add one extra 20 px epoch at the start (3x20+3x24+2x28+4x32, 12 epochs, LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps; same 20 px graph, no new shapes). Change nothing else. The 20 px epoch is the cheapest epoch (~0.43 s), and E031 showed that early-phase optimizer step count matters under Muon. So extra early steps may buy as much accuracy per second as the 32 px tail at roughly equal cost.

Exploit and test the FixRes mechanism: the closing full-res phase only needs to re-fit BN stats and the head, so it can be shorter. On the current incumbent (E030, or the low-res-epoch variant if that run is kept), move one 32 px epoch to 28 px: 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32 (11 epochs, same LR schedule over total steps, same 4 graphs). Change nothing else. Run salt 0 and salt 1 and compare against the pooled estimate, since the expected effect is near the noise.

Rebase of I040 onto the current incumbent. On E030, raise label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.4 in all phases and change nothing else. ls is a graph constant, so recapture all 4 graphs in build. E012 (0.3 -> 0.2 lost 0.21 pp) suggests the optimum may sit at or above 0.3 for 100 classes in an under-fit 11-epoch schedule. This is the last untested direction of the ls knob, and it is time-free.
salt-1 companion of E038 (ls 0.4; calibration only, never kept)

Explore an untested Muon knob: momentum. E028 showed lr is flat over 0.205-0.256, but momentum 0.655 is inherited from Hiverge's CIFAR-10 3/3/3 net without resizing or AOL. On E030, raise the Muon momentum from 0.655 to 0.75 (Nesterov form unchanged) and keep lr, the SGD groups, the schedule, Lookahead and resolutions fixed. Momentum is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Rationale: E031 showed the early phase is step-limited; higher momentum smooths the orthogonalized direction across consecutive small-batch steps, which may raise per-step progress.

Exploit, a numerically equivalent throughput cut. On the current tip (E038: 2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 0.7546 @ 6.68 s), replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(2), or an equivalent amax over dims (2,3), in every resolution's forward. Change nothing else. Recapture all 4 CUDA graphs and the eval path in build. Confirm that eval still returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. In the smoke test, log ms/step per phase and a one-step profiler line for the pooling backward kernel (atomic adaptive_max_pool2d_backward vs the amax backward).

Exploit, a numerically equivalent throughput cut. On the current tip (E038: 2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 0.7546 @ 6.68 s), replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(2), or an equivalent amax over dims (2,3), in every resolution's forward. Change nothing else. Recapture all 4 CUDA graphs and the eval path in build. Confirm that eval still returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. In the smoke test, log ms/step per phase and a one-step profiler line for the pooling backward kernel (atomic adaptive_max_pool2d_backward vs the amax backward).

Exploit and add margin by fixing a BN-statistics mismatch (D004 C0031/C0035). Lookahead copies the slow weights into the model at the end of training, but the BN running statistics were accumulated under the fast iterates, and the frozen block's stats under the detach regime. At the end of train(), after the final Lookahead sync, reset all BN running stats. Re-estimate them with cumulative averaging (momentum=None) from 6 forward-only batches of 1536 un-augmented, un-flipped 32 px training images (no_grad, fp16, channels_last). Draw the images with the trial-seeded generator, then restore BN momentum. Do the re-estimation pass in a small CUDA graph or compiled function warmed up in build on synthetic data, so its first call costs nothing extra in the timed region. Training data only; the test set is never touched. Change nothing else on E038. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

Exploit and buy margin through cheap deep capacity, at equal epochs (the test E008 confounded). On E038, widen group 3 from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768) at every resolution and adjust the head input to match. Keep epochs, resolution schedule, LR schedule, Muon lr/momentum, ls 0.4, freezing and the whitening-bias window fixed. Recapture all 4 graphs in build. Log ms/step per phase. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

Exploit, removing low-res backward work. On E038, train the whitening-conv bias for only the first ~0.25 epoch (8 steps at batch 1536), as Fable and Hiverge do, instead of the first 5 epochs. After that, detach the whitening output (after its activation) in every phase, including 20 and 24 px. The 20/24 px phases then also skip the first group-1 conv's dgrad and the whitening BN/activation backward. Capture a no-detach 20 px graph for the first 8 steps plus the detached 20/24 px graphs in build, so nothing is captured in the timed region (5 graphs in total). Drop the whitening bias from the optimizer, or zero its lr, after step 8. Change nothing else.

Calibration (no recipe change), to set the keep rule. Using the existing internal salt / trial-seed plumbing, run the E038 tip recipe on dev seeds 3-12 outside the official command (10 trials, same code), and log per-seed accuracy and time. Nothing is kept from this run. The result replaces the 2-salt guesses with a 10-seed estimate of the recipe's true mean and per-seed std, and tests whether official seeds 0-2 are a favourable draw: salt-1 draws came in lower three times (E027, E034, E039).

Exploit, a kernel-efficiency cut in the most expensive phase. On E038, during the 4 epochs at 32 px, switch the frozen first group-1 block's BatchNorm to eval mode: it uses fixed running stats, gets no batch-stat reductions and no stat updates. Before entering the 32 px phase, re-estimate that one BN's running stats from 2 forward-only 32 px training batches (cumulative average), so its fixed affine matches the 32 px input distribution. Fold it into a per-channel scale/shift fused after the conv if inductor allows. Capture the modified 32 px graph and the tiny re-estimation pass in build. Change nothing else.

Exploit by stacking two near-misses. On E038 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3, Muon with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) Re-apply E042's pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax, because amax crashed in E041. (2) Add E043's end-of-train BN re-estimation with 4 batches instead of 6. After the final Lookahead sync, reset all BN running stats. Re-estimate them with momentum=None from 4 forward-only batches of 1536 un-augmented 32 px training images, drawn with the trial-seeded generator, under no_grad, fp16 and channels_last. Then restore BN momentum. Put the re-estimation pass in a small graph or compiled function warmed up in build on synthetic data. Recapture all 4 train graphs in build. Check that eval gives finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Besides the official run, evaluate the same code on dev seeds 3-12 outside the official command, so the BN-re-estimation gain is measured against E046's 10-seed baseline of 0.7534 with SE about 0.09 pp, not against a single draw.

Exploit, removing low-res backward work at a phase boundary, so no new graph is needed. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), train the whitening-conv bias only during the 20 px phase (epochs 1-2, about 64 steps) instead of epochs 1-5. In the 24 px phase, detach the whitening output (after its activation) before group 1, as the 28/32 px graphs already do, and zero the whitening bias lr or drop it from that phase's parameter list. The 24 px graph is recaptured in build with the detach. The 20 px graph is unchanged and the graph count stays 4. This is the 2-epoch window between E045's 8 steps (failed, -0.47 pp) and E029's 3 epochs (neutral), aligned with the 20->24 px boundary. Also evaluate dev seeds 3-12. Log ms/step in the 24 px phase.

Exploit, extending the FreezeOut-style cut. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), also freeze the first group-1 conv block (whitening-output -> 128 conv, pool, BN, GELU) during the 2 epochs at 28 px, exactly as already done at 32 px. In the 28 px graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv. Drop that conv's weight and BN affine params from the 28 px phase's Muon/SGD lists, or zero their lr. BN stays in train mode. Recapture the 28 px graph in build; the graph count is unchanged. conv1 is then trained only in the 5 epochs at 20/24 px. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 alongside the official run. Log ms/step per phase.

Exploit, buying margin through the smallest group-3 capacity step. Before the official run, microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group-3 widths 576 and 640. Do not reuse E004/E044 deltas: the E044 post-mortem showed that the cost structure has shifted. If 640 costs <=+4% ms/step, then on the current tip (with the pooling cut) widen group 3 from 576 to 640 at every resolution and adjust the head input. Hold epochs, resolutions, LR schedule, Muon lr/momentum, ls, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark shows >+5%, log it and do not run.

Explore a margin source inside Muon at no time cost. On E038, replace the 2 fixed quintic NS steps that follow AOL preconditioning with Polar Express per-iteration minimax coefficients for 2 iterations (arXiv 2505.16932), with the lower singular-value bound set to ~1e-3 and the safety factor from the paper. AOL already bounds sigma_max <= 1. Use the same matmul count, the same lr 0.205, momentum 0.655 and per-step renorm. Before running, validate offline on 3 real momentum-gradient matrices captured from a dev training step (not Gaussian; the E035 lesson) that the smallest decile of singular values is lifted higher than with the current coefficients. Recapture all graphs in build. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

Explore an output knob that has never been swept and costs nothing. On E038 (ls 0.4), multiply the head's fixed output scale (the airbench 1/9-style logit multiplier, rescaled for 100 classes) by 2x and change nothing else. The scale is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Run salt 0 and salt 1. Contingency: if the 2-salt mean falls by >=0.15 pp, run 0.5x next. Larger smoothing (ls 0.4) lowers the optimal logit magnitude, so the scale and ls interact.

Explore an SGD-era knob never varied under Muon. Note: with per-step weight renorm, weight decay on the Muon conv group is effectively a no-op, so the live knobs are the SGD-group settings. On E038 (or the current tip), halve the BN-bias lr multiplier from 64x to 32x, and change nothing else. Keep Muon lr/momentum, head lr, wd, the schedule and Lookahead fixed. The multiplier lives in the per-group lr. If it is folded into the GPU schedule tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture in build. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 plus official seeds. Contingency: if the dev mean falls by >=0.15 pp, run 128x next.

Exploit: spend E053's margin on the two time cuts already measured as accuracy-neutral on dev seeds. On E053 (E038 + head output scale 2x, ls 0.4; official 0.7575, dev 0.7578 @ 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) The pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax (amax crashed in E041). (2) E049's 2-epoch whitening-bias window: train the whitening-conv bias only in the 20 px phase, and in the 24 px graph detach the whitening output after its activation and zero the bias lr. Keep the graph count at 4, recapture everything in build, and change nothing else. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.

Exploit, the next banked cut, stacked on the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E053). Move one 32 px epoch to 28 px, giving 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32: 11 epochs, the LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps, the same 4 graphs. The 28 px graph keeps conv1 trainable, as now (E050 showed conv1 needs its 28 px updates). Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12, and compare against the tip's own dev mean.

Explore, continuing the only margin source found since E030. On the current tip (A's stack if kept, else E053), raise the head's fixed output scale from 2x to 3x the original airbench-derived value. ls stays 0.4 and nothing else changes. The scale is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Contingency: if dev rises >=0.15 pp, try 4x next. If it falls >=0.15 pp, 2x is near the optimum; then test ls 0.3 at 2x scale, since the scale and ls interact.

Explore, a diagnostic only, run outside the official command and the timed region, with no recipe change. Test accuracy is logged as usual. Nothing is kept. This tells us whether the head-scale gain came from better fit or less over-regularization, and whether the recipe under-fits (margin from steps or capacity) or has a large gap (margin from regularization).

Exploit, work removal in group 3, extending E059's finding that one 8x8 group-2 conv cost ~0.73 s for only -0.15 pp. First microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group 3 at 3 vs 2 convs. If the 2-conv version saves >=4%, cut group 3 from 3 convs to 2 (net 2/2/2, airbench94-style) at width 576, keeping the pooling position and head. Explore whether anchor-fixed low-res steps buy margin, rebased onto the 2/2/3 net, where an epoch is now much cheaper. On the E059 tip, add one 20 px epoch at the start (3x20+3x24+3x28+2.5x32). Exploit: width-based work removal in group 2, the cheapest remaining structural lever now that the depth floors are reached. Exploit, separating the two knobs that E053 confounded. On the E061 tip, keep the head output scale at 2x and halve the head-weight lr (in the SGD head group), changing nothing else. Under Agarwala et al., the effective head lr scales as lr·β², so the 2x scale also quadrupled the effective head step. Halving the lr tests whether part of E053's +0.44 pp came from temperature and part was a too-large head step. The lr is a per-group value in the schedule tensor, so recapture only if it is a graph constant. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Contingency: if dev falls by 0.15 pp or more, run 2x head lr next. If |Δ| < 0.1 pp, the head lr is not a live knob at this scale; close H1.10.2.

Calibration against the winner's curse, with no recipe change and nothing kept.
